utterances.text: I just want to then deal with one aspect of this -- from your listening. The intercepts which you have listened to, which you listened to here, they reflected, did they, particularly the ones where you were referred to, the situation at the time? Did you get the interpretation?

utterances.speaker: NEDJO VLASKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I have too much noise in my earphones. It's a problem. Perhaps we're being listened in.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: [Microphone not activated]

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Right. Did you hear the question?

utterances.speaker: NEDJO VLASKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't. I didn't hear the question because there's too much noise in my earphones.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... the usher can give you another set and see if that's any better. The question I asked, Mr. Vlaski, was this: You listened to a number of intercepts that particularly dealt with your situation but also referred to other matters. Did those conversations, and forget whether they were legal or illegally taped, represent a reflection on events that you knew about?

utterances.speaker: NEDJO VLASKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: From what I could hear and read, I believe that they did reflect. There were many more things, of course. You don’t have insight into all the intercepts, only the ones that were presented to you.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: I accept that entirely. All right. Sorry, one last matter. You were asked by Mr. Zecevic yesterday, and you had never said anything about the meeting but he put to you, at page 6406: "It was because of the nature of the your work that you were informed of the secret meeting of the SDA in the police hall which was held on 26th of May, 1991; is that right?" Now you have never mentioned the meeting of the 26th of May in interview, in Banja Luka, nor when you gave evidence when I was asking you questions, but you knew exactly what Mr. Zecevic was talking about. Did he discuss this with you when you met?

utterances.speaker: NEDJO VLASKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, not this topic. But it was only logical that this issue of organising would crop up, because the context of my testimony had to do with the response to various actions by the Party of Democratic Action.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: What I want to know, Mr. Vlaski, is you didn't appear surprised by the question at all. And so that's why I'm asking you whether you discussed this with Mr. Zecevic when you met him.

utterances.speaker: NEDJO VLASKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I wasn't surprised by a single question put to me during my testimony here. I am not surprised.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Yes. All right. You see, you then -- your answer to this was: "Yes, because at the time I was the chief of the administration for the security of individual and those individuals included Mr. Izetbegovic, who participated in the meeting." Do we understand that you -- because were responsible for the security, particularly of the President, you accompanied Mr. Izetbegovic to this secret meeting?

utterances.speaker: NEDJO VLASKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I wasn't Mr. Izetbegovic's body-guard. I was the chief of the administration. The practice at the time when I headed the administration was such that many attempts were made at trying to prevent me from obtaining relevant information as to when Mr. Izetbegovic was taking the trip, where, when he was going to come back, and who he was going to stay when and who with. And as for this particular meeting, I received the relevant information perhaps 15 minutes ahead of its commencement.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: All right. Because, obviously, whoever was his body-guard, who was under your command had to say where he was going and with whom?

utterances.speaker: NEDJO VLASKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: He had body-guards who were not under our control. They were party people. Some of them were held criminally liable later on, and some even earlier on.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Anyway, the upshot is, whether it was 15 minutes before or at another stage, you were aware that Mr. Izetbegovic was going to a hall to attend the meeting of the SDA; is that right?

utterances.speaker: NEDJO VLASKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's right. Because the meeting was somewhat broader. It included the representatives from Sandzak, Croatia, Serbia, and all over Bosnia, probably also from abroad.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: I have no further questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: When the Chamber gave leave to the Prosecution to cross-examine this witness in -- in the course of re-examination, it was alerted to the possibility that this may have -- this unusual course, may have resulted in leave being given to the counsel for the Defence to further cross-examine. But inasmuch as Ms. Korner has confined herself to matters that arose out of counsel's cross-examination, I -- do I correctly conclude that the question of further cross-examination does not really arise?

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: You're correct, Your Honours. We don't have any questions for this witness anymore.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: I have no further questions for this witness, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Mr. Vlaski, yesterday you told us, and it was repeated today, that it seems that for Bosnia-Herzegovina, the relationship between the master and the servant was a historical category and they believed that it was time for them to become masters. So I presume that, before that, they were the servants?

utterances.speaker: NEDJO VLASKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, it doesn't only have to do with servants. You've gone to one extremism. We had equality, we had equality in the Socialist Republic -- Federative Republic of Yugoslavia. That was the principle in which the country was based and servants and masters were a historical occurrence during the Ottoman Empire.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Mr. Vlaski, we thank you for your assistance to the Tribunal in coming to give evidence. Your testimony is now at an end, and you're now released as a witness. The Chamber will now rise, and we will resume at 2.15 tomorrow afternoon.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: to be reconvened on Thursday, the 18th day of February, 2010, at 2.15 p.m.

procedural_notes.text: --- Whereupon the hearing adjourned at 4.56 p.m.,
